Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 36, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Ya-Sin because Allah the Exalted began it with this utterance, so this surah stands alone in this construction and is distinguished by it from the rest of the surahs.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• An oath affirming the truthfulness of the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), a discussion of the disbelievers of Makkah who denied the Prophet (ﷺ), and an explanation of the reward of those who follow the Prophet (ﷺ) and benefit from the warning.

• Mention of the signs of Allah's power through the diverse cosmic phenomena, to establish the Oneness of Allah the Exalted, and emphasis on the reality of resurrection and gathering.

• A discussion of the Resurrection and its terrors, such as the Blast of Terror (nafkhat al-faza') and the Blast of Swooning (nafkhat al-sa'q), and a discussion of the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, and a reminder of the covenant Allah made with them, which He placed in their innate nature (fitrah): to keep away from the path of evil and to follow the call to good.

• Affirmation of the truthfulness of the Messenger (ﷺ) and of the Book that he brought, and consolation for him so that what the opposing polytheists say does not grieve him, for Allah knows their secret and their public speech; and implicit in this is a threat to the opponents.

[Tafsir]

This is the commentary on Surah Yasin (36), verse 11, from al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (the King Fahd Complex's commentary):

Your warning only benefits the one who believes in the Qur'an and follows what it contains of the commands of Allah, and fears the Most Merciful (al-Rahman) in private, where no one sees him except Allah. So give him good news of forgiveness from Allah for his sins, and of a reward from Him in the Hereafter for his righteous deeds, which is his entry into Paradise.

Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, all of them, by resurrecting them on the Day of Resurrection, and We record what they did of good and evil, and their traces which they caused in their lifetime and after their death, of good, such as a righteous child, beneficial knowledge, and ongoing charity, and of evil, such as associating partners with God and disobedience. And everything We have enumerated in a clear Book, which is the Mother of Books, to which it returns, and it is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). So it is incumbent upon the intelligent person to take account of himself, so that he may be an example of goodness in his lifetime and after his death.

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 36, verse 28:**

The matter did not require sending down an army from the sky to punish them, after they killed the man who advised them sincerely and denied their messengers. They are weaker and more insignificant than that. We would not send down angels upon nations when We destroy them. Rather, We send upon them a punishment that annihilates them.
The destruction of them was only by a single blast, and at once they were dead, not one of them left alive.
Alas for the servants, and their remorse on the Day of Resurrection, when they witness the punishment! No messenger comes to them from Allah, the Exalted, but they used to mock him and ridicule him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 36, verse 34:

﴿And We made in it gardens of date palms and grapevines, and We caused springs to gush forth within it.﴾

All of that is so that the servants may eat of its fruit. And this is nothing but the mercy of God toward them, not by their striving nor their toil, nor by their own power and strength. Will they not then thank God for the blessings He has bestowed upon them, these favors that cannot be counted or enumerated?

Glory be to Allah, the Mighty, who created all the kinds (al-asnaf) of the plant species of the earth, and of themselves, male and female, and of other creatures of Allah that they do not know. He alone has the sole right to create, so none other than Him should be associated with Him in worship.
And a sign for them, indicating the oneness of God and the perfection of His power: this night, from which We strip away the day, and then the people are in darkness.

The sun also is a sign for them: it runs on its course toward a fixed place of rest that Allah has appointed for it, which it neither overshoots nor falls short of. That is the decree of the All-Mighty, whom none can overcome, the All-Knowing, from whose knowledge nothing is hidden.

We have also made the moon a sign in its creation, and We have determined for it stations, so that it changes each night. It begins as a thin crescent, then grows until it becomes a full, round moon. Then it returns thin, like the old date-palm stalk (ʿidq) that is curved in its thinness, its bending, and its yellowness, because of its age and dryness.

For each of the sun, the moon, the night and the day there is a time that Allah has decreed for it, which it does not overstep. So the sun cannot catch up with the moon and obliterate its light or alter its course, and the night cannot outrun the day and enter upon it before its time has ended. Each of the sun, the moon and the stars is in an orbit, swimming along.

A proof for them and an argument that Allah alone deserves to be worshipped, the One who bestows favors, is that We carried those among the descendants of Adam who were saved in Noah's ship, which was filled with all kinds of created beings, so that life would continue after the flood.
And We have created for these polytheists and others the like of Noah's ship, among the boats and other vessels that they ride, which carry them to their homelands.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 36, verse 44:

Except that We show them mercy, so We save them and let them enjoy [worldly life] for an appointed term, so that they may return [to obedience] and make up for what they neglected.

When it is said to the polytheists: "Beware of the matter of the Hereafter and its terrors, and of the affairs of this world and its punishment, in the hope that you may receive the mercy of Allah," they turn away and do not respond to that.

And there does not come to these polytheists any sign clear from their Lord, one that would guide them to the truth and make plain to them the truthfulness of the Messenger, except that they turn away from it and do not benefit from it.

And when it is said to the disbelievers, "Spend from what Allah has provided you," the disbelievers say to the believers, arguing against them, "Shall we feed the one whom Allah, if He willed, would have fed? You (O believers) are only in clear error, for you are ordering us to do this."
And these disbelievers say, mocking and hastening [the matter]: "When will this resurrection take place, if you are truthful in what you say about it?"

What are these polytheists, who hasten the threat of God against them, waiting for except the blast of terror at the establishment of the Hour? It will seize them suddenly while they are disputing about the affairs of their lives.

So these polytheists, at the blowing of the trumpet (al-qarn), will be unable to make any bequest to anyone, nor will they be able to return to their families. Rather, they will die in their markets and in their places.
And the second blast is blown on the "Qarn" (the trumpet), so their souls are returned to their bodies, and they come out from their graves toward their Lord, hastening.

The disbelievers in the resurrection will say, full of regret: "Woe to us! Who has raised us up from our graves?" They will be answered, and it will be said to them: "This is what the Most Merciful promised, and what the truthful messengers reported."

The raising from the graves will be nothing more than the result of a single blast on the "Qarn" (the Trumpet), and then all of creation will be brought before Us, present for reckoning and recompense.

On that Day, the reckoning will be carried out with justice: no soul will be wronged in the least, through a reduction of its good deeds or an increase in its evil deeds, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do in the worldly life.
